models.deep.attention module¶

Attention Mechanisms and Transformers.

Custom attention implementations: - AttentionNetwork (Generic Attention mechanism) - NSTransformer (Non-Stationary Transformer)

class models.deep.attention.AttentionNetwork(input_dim: int, d_model: int = 128, num_layers: int = 4, num_heads: int = 8, d_ff: int = 512, output_dim: int = 10, dropout: float = 0.1, max_seq_len: int = 1000, output_type: Literal['prediction', 'embedding'] = 'prediction')[source]¶

Bases: Module

Attention Network for sequence modeling.

A stack of attention blocks that process sequences using self-attention mechanisms.

Parameters:

  • input_dim – Input feature dimension

  • d_model – Model dimension

  • num_layers – Number of attention blocks

  • num_heads – Number of attention heads per block

  • d_ff – Feed-forward dimension

  • output_dim – Output dimension

  • dropout – Dropout probability

  • max_seq_len – Maximum sequence length (for positional encoding)

  • output_type – ‘prediction’ returns final output, ‘embedding’ returns features

  • device – Device to create mask on

  • mask – Optional attention mask

  • return_sequence – If True, return output for each timestep

Returns:

Output tensor of shape (batch_size, output_dim) or (batch_size, seq_len, output_dim)

class models.deep.autoencoders.VAE(input_dim: int, latent_dim: int, d_model: int = 128, seq_len: int = 100, pred_len: int = 20, encoder_type: Literal['transformer', 'mamba', 'lstm', 'gru', 'xlstm'] = 'mamba', decoder_type: Literal['transformer', 'mamba', 'lstm', 'gru', 'xlstm'] | None = None, n_layers: int = 3, n_heads: int = 8, d_ff: int = 512, dropout: float = 0.1, activation: str = 'gelu', encoder_kwargs: dict | None = None, decoder_kwargs: dict | None = None)[source]¶

Bases: Module

Variational Auto-Encoder for time series prediction.

Architecture: - Encoder: TimeSeriesBackbone (Transformer/Mamba/LSTM/etc.) → latent mean & log_variance - Reparameterization: Sample from N(mean, variance) using the reparameterization trick - Decoder: Latent vector → TimeSeriesBackbone → reconstructed sequence

Parameters:

  • input_dim – Number of input features

  • latent_dim – Dimensionality of the latent space

  • d_model – Hidden dimension for the backbone models

  • seq_len – Input sequence length

  • pred_len – Prediction/output sequence length

  • encoder_type – Type of encoder backbone (‘transformer’, ‘mamba’, ‘lstm’, ‘gru’, ‘xlstm’)

  • decoder_type – Type of decoder backbone (defaults to same as encoder)

  • n_layers – Number of layers in encoder/decoder

  • n_heads – Number of attention heads (for Transformer)

  • d_ff – Feed-forward dimension (for Transformer)

  • dropout – Dropout rate

  • activation – Activation function for Transformer

  • encoder_kwargs – Additional kwargs for encoder backbone

  • decoder_kwargs – Additional kwargs for decoder backbone

class models.deep.competitive.LVQ(input_dim, num_classes, prototypes_per_class=1, output_type='prediction')[source]¶

Bases: Module

Learning Vector Quantization (LVQ) implementation. A prototype-based supervised classification algorithm.

forward(x, return_embedding=False)[source]¶

Forward pass finds the nearest prototype. In inference, this performs classification. In training, custom training loop is needed for LVQ updates, or we can approximate with soft competitive learning.

training_step(x, y)[source]¶

LVQ specific training step (LVQ1 rule). This updates prototypes manually as LVQ is non-gradient based primarily. However, for PyTorch compatibility, we might expose a loss.

class models.deep.convolutional.DeepResNet(input_dim: int, hidden_dim: int = 128, num_blocks: int = 4, output_dim: int = 10, use_conv: bool = False, dropout: float = 0.1, kernel_size: int = 3, output_type: Literal['prediction', 'embedding'] = 'prediction')[source]¶

Bases: Module

Deep Residual Network (ResNet) for time series or sequence data.

ResNet uses skip connections to enable training of very deep networks by addressing the vanishing gradient problem.

Parameters:

  • input_dim – Input feature dimension

  • hidden_dim – Hidden dimension for residual blocks

  • num_blocks – Number of residual blocks

  • output_dim – Output dimension

  • use_conv – If True, use convolutional blocks; otherwise use fully connected

  • dropout – Dropout probability

  • output_type – ‘prediction’ returns final output, ‘embedding’ returns features

class models.deep.general.NeuralODE(input_dim: int, hidden_dim: int = 64, output_dim: int = 1, num_layers: int = 2, time_steps: int = 10, horizon: float = 1.0, output_type: str = 'prediction')[source]¶

Bases: Module

Neural Ordinary Differential Equation Model.

The model predicts the evolution of a state ‘z’ over time: dz/dt = f(z, t, theta)

where f is a neural network.

Parameters:

  • input_dim – Dimension of the state z.

  • hidden_dim – Hidden dimension of the derivative network.

  • output_dim – Output dimension (can be different if we project at the end).

  • time_steps – Number of time steps to simulate (default 10).

  • horizon – Time horizon (default 1.0).

forward(x: Tensor, t: Tensor | None = None) → Tensor[source]¶

Forward pass.

Parameters:

  • x – Initial state (batch_size, input_dim).

  • t – Time points (num_steps,). Defaults to linspace(0, horizon, time_steps).

Returns:

trajectory or prediction.

class models.deep.general.PINN(input_dim: int, hidden_dim: int = 20, output_dim: int = 1, num_layers: int = 4, activation: str = 'tanh', output_type: str = 'prediction')[source]¶

Bases: Module

Physics-Informed Neural Network.

A fully connected network that approximates a solution u(x, t) to a PDE. Includes methods to easily compute derivatives du/dx, du/dt, d^2u/dx^2, etc.

Parameters:

  • input_dim – Dimension of domain (e.g., 2 for x and t).

  • hidden_dim – Number of neurons per layer.

  • output_dim – Dimension of solution u (e.g., 1 for scalar field).

  • num_layers – Number of hidden layers.

  • activation – Activation function (tanh is standard for PINNs due to smoothness).

forward(x: Tensor) → Tensor[source]¶

Forward pass.

Parameters:

x – Collocation points (batch_size, input_dim). Requires requires_grad=True if computing physics loss outside.

gradient(u: Tensor, x: Tensor) → Tensor[source]¶

Compute gradient du/dx.

Parameters:

  • u – Output tensor (batch_size, output_dim).

  • x – Input tensor (batch_size, input_dim).

Returns:

Gradient tensor (batch_size, input_dim).

Return type:

grad

laplacian(u: Tensor, x: Tensor) → Tensor[source]¶

Compute Laplacian (sum of second derivatives). Note: This is expensive (O(d^2) or O(d) depending on implementation). For input_dim=1 (time), it is just d^2u/dt^2.

models.deep.spiking module¶

Spiking Neural Network (SNN) Components.

Provides implementations of Spiking Neural Networks elements such as Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) cells and surrogate gradient functions for training SNNs with backpropagation.

class models.deep.spiking.LIFCell(input_dim, hidden_dim, decay=0.9, threshold=1.0, alpha=25.0)[source]¶

Bases: Module

Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) Neuron Cell.

Dynamics: U[t] = decay * U[t-1] + W X[t] - S[t-1] * threshold S[t] = Heaviside(U[t] - threshold)

forward(x, state=None)[source]¶
Parameters:

  • x – Input tensor (Batch, Input_Dim)

  • state – Tuple (u, s) of previous membrane potential and spike. If None, initialized to zeros.

Returns:

Spikes at current time step (Batch, Hidden_Dim) state_next: (u_next, s_next)

Return type:

s_next

Bases: Module

Learning Vector Quantization (LVQ) implementation. A prototype-based supervised classification algorithm.

forward(x, return_embedding=False)[source]¶

Forward pass finds the nearest prototype. In inference, this performs classification. In training, custom training loop is needed for LVQ updates, or we can approximate with soft competitive learning.

training_step(x, y)[source]¶

LVQ specific training step (LVQ1 rule). This updates prototypes manually as LVQ is non-gradient based primarily. However, for PyTorch compatibility, we might expose a loss.

class models.deep.NeuralODE(input_dim: int, hidden_dim: int = 64, output_dim: int = 1, num_layers: int = 2, time_steps: int = 10, horizon: float = 1.0, output_type: str = 'prediction')[source]¶

Bases: Module

Neural Ordinary Differential Equation Model.

The model predicts the evolution of a state ‘z’ over time: dz/dt = f(z, t, theta)

where f is a neural network.

Parameters:

  • input_dim – Dimension of the state z.

  • hidden_dim – Hidden dimension of the derivative network.

  • output_dim – Output dimension (can be different if we project at the end).

  • time_steps – Number of time steps to simulate (default 10).

  • horizon – Time horizon (default 1.0).

Forward pass.

Parameters:

  • x – Initial state (batch_size, input_dim).

  • t – Time points (num_steps,). Defaults to linspace(0, horizon, time_steps).

Returns:

trajectory or prediction.

class models.deep.PINN(input_dim: int, hidden_dim: int = 20, output_dim: int = 1, num_layers: int = 4, activation: str = 'tanh', output_type: str = 'prediction')[source]¶

Bases: Module

Physics-Informed Neural Network.

A fully connected network that approximates a solution u(x, t) to a PDE. Includes methods to easily compute derivatives du/dx, du/dt, d^2u/dx^2, etc.

Parameters:

  • input_dim – Dimension of domain (e.g., 2 for x and t).

  • hidden_dim – Number of neurons per layer.

  • output_dim – Dimension of solution u (e.g., 1 for scalar field).

  • num_layers – Number of hidden layers.

  • activation – Activation function (tanh is standard for PINNs due to smoothness).

forward(x: Tensor) → Tensor[source]¶

Forward pass.

Parameters:

x – Collocation points (batch_size, input_dim). Requires requires_grad=True if computing physics loss outside.

grad

laplacian(u: Tensor, x: Tensor) → Tensor[source]¶

Compute Laplacian (sum of second derivatives). Note: This is expensive (O(d^2) or O(d) depending on implementation). For input_dim=1 (time), it is just d^2u/dt^2.

class models.deep.VAE(input_dim: int, latent_dim: int, d_model: int = 128, seq_len: int = 100, pred_len: int = 20, encoder_type: Literal['transformer', 'mamba', 'lstm', 'gru', 'xlstm'] = 'mamba', decoder_type: Literal['transformer', 'mamba', 'lstm', 'gru', 'xlstm'] | None = None, n_layers: int = 3, n_heads: int = 8, d_ff: int = 512, dropout: float = 0.1, activation: str = 'gelu', encoder_kwargs: dict | None = None, decoder_kwargs: dict | None = None)[source]¶

Bases: Module

Variational Auto-Encoder for time series prediction.

Architecture: - Encoder: TimeSeriesBackbone (Transformer/Mamba/LSTM/etc.) → latent mean & log_variance - Reparameterization: Sample from N(mean, variance) using the reparameterization trick - Decoder: Latent vector → TimeSeriesBackbone → reconstructed sequence

Parameters:

  • input_dim – Number of input features

  • latent_dim – Dimensionality of the latent space

  • d_model – Hidden dimension for the backbone models

  • seq_len – Input sequence length

  • pred_len – Prediction/output sequence length

  • encoder_type – Type of encoder backbone (‘transformer’, ‘mamba’, ‘lstm’, ‘gru’, ‘xlstm’)

  • decoder_type – Type of decoder backbone (defaults to same as encoder)

  • n_layers – Number of layers in encoder/decoder

  • n_heads – Number of attention heads (for Transformer)

  • d_ff – Feed-forward dimension (for Transformer)

  • dropout – Dropout rate

  • activation – Activation function for Transformer

  • encoder_kwargs – Additional kwargs for encoder backbone

  • decoder_kwargs – Additional kwargs for decoder backbone

z – Latent vector of shape (batch_size, latent_dim)
